target.title: fix(node-host): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in runCommand
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`runCommand` in `src/node-host/invoke.ts` captures child-process stdout/stderr but only attaches `"data"` listeners. If either stream emits an `"error"` event (e.g. EPIPE after the child exits abruptly, or stream destruction during process teardown), the error is unhandled and can crash the node-host process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `"error"` listeners to `child.stdout` and `child.stderr` that record the stream error, terminate the child, and let the `exit` handler finalize with the error message. This keeps child exit/close authoritative for `system.run` completion while still preventing the unhandled stream error from crashing the node-host process.

## User Impact

Node-host `system.run` invocations that previously could crash on stream teardown now return a failed result with the error message instead of taking down the process.

## Evidence

Regression tests:

```bash
pnpm test src/node-host/invoke.run-command.test.ts
```

```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  2 passed (2)
```

Real behavior proof:

```bash
node_modules/.bin/tsx scripts/proof/node-host-run-command-stream-errors.mts
```

```
=== Proof: node-host runCommand stream error handling ===

Result: success=false, error=stdout read failed

PASS: stream errors were caught and runCommand returned a failed result.
```
